rev.why: All numbers checked against Table 2, Table 3 (Advanced Claude row rebuilt: 77.3 / 74.1 / 0.96 holds) and the text. The works/partly/does-not-work thresholds (85% / 65%) are the draft's own, not set by the protocol or the authors; verdicts near a threshold (Claude Opus without skill 84.6, Qwen without skill 64.7, DeepSeek without skill 63.4) could go either way. Author to confirm the rule.

Round 1 gave the without-skill configurations no cost verdict ('baseline') and justified the with-skill cost verdicts by the paired ratio, i.e. against the baseline, which §6 rules out (each configuration judged on its own). Cost now judged on each configuration's own output tokens per unit RPR (28.8-82.0K, Table 3); 'works' is the extractor's judgement, since only an output-token proxy is reported and no threshold is set. All RPR and token values re-checked against Tables 2-3 (Advanced Claude Opus row of Table 3 rebuilt: 77.3 / 74.1 / 0.96 holds). Quality thresholds remain the extractor's; verdicts near 85% / 65% (Claude Opus without skill 84.6, Qwen without skill 64.7, DeepSeek without skill 63.4) could go either way.

All RPR values re-checked against Table 2 Avg. columns and all tokens/RPR values against Table 3 Avg. columns (Advanced Claude Opus row rebuilt from the jumbled table: product values average to 77.3 / 74.1, ratio 0.96, so the values hold); with-skill overall means match p. 10 and the computed without-skill means are correct. The verdicts are judgements: quality thresholds (85% / 65%) are the extractor's, with Claude Opus without skill (84.6), Qwen without skill (64.7) and DeepSeek without skill (63.4) close to a boundary; cost 'works' for every configuration rests only on an output-token proxy the authors say is not a cost estimate (p. 12), with no time or money reported.

fields.v: Tasks: 18 task instances (9 projects x Basic/Advanced). Configurations: 6 models x {without skill, with skill} in Claude Code 2.1.200. Baseline: without skill. Held constant: agent, project, instruction, execution environment (fresh Docker container per trial), rubrics and evaluators. Acceptance tests: rubric-derived static, unit, integration, E2E checks + LLM-assisted criteria. Repetitions: 'repeated trials' averaged per task instance, number Not stated. Human intervention: none stated

With skill improves mean RPR by +10.31 points on average; positive in 101 of 108 model-product-scenario cells (4 lower, 3 unchanged); Basic +11.27 vs Advanced +9.35; per model +6.81 (Claude Opus 4.8) to +15.51 (Kimi K2.7 Code). Larger gains when baseline < 40% (+17.64) than 80-100% (+4.52). Output tokens per unit RPR lower with skill in all 12 model-scenario aggregates (ratio 0.69-0.96, mean 0.81), but > 1 in some product cells. Model ranking with skill: Claude Opus 4.8 91.37% > GLM-5.2 87.12 > Kimi 82.18 > Qwen 75.78 > DeepSeek 75.23 > MiniMax 68.58. No significance tests

Distinguished conditions and models; method-level diagnostics separate structural completion (static 92.79% Basic) from executable behavior (integration 73.16%, E2E 78.24%) and domain requirements (Advanced E2E 97.03% vs LLM 61.05%). Repeatability: fresh containers; number of trials and variance not reported. Limitations stated: results grounded in Alipay products, these tasks and agent configurations; LLM rubric verification noted as noisy in related work; method scores cover different rubric subsets

Results limited to Alipay Open Platform products, the 18 task instances and the coding-agent configuration studied; ceiling effect possible at high baselines; output-token metric is only a relative generation-efficiency measure. Future: more models and agent frameworks, broader repository coverage, longer-horizon executable payment workflows

Code public: github.com/inclusionAI/PIBench. No pre-registration. Languages: JavaScript/TypeScript, PHP, Java. Inconsistencies: Fig. 3 includes a 'Kimi K3' row not mentioned in the text or Table 2; product names differ between text and tables (App / In-App, Pre-Authorization / Auth., Barcode / Order QR); Fig. 1 project names (edoc, SaaS Starter) differ slightly from Table 1, and the text cites repositories (Hi.Events, opensourcepos) not listed in Table 1. Number of trials per configuration and LLM judge model not stated. Tables 1-3 extracted with jumbled columns; Table 3 Advanced Claude row rebuilt by ratio check (77.3 -> 74.1, 0.96). Overall without-skill means computed by this draft from Table 2. Authors are the vendor of the evaluated skill
